methodological_rigor.justification: The study leverages a pre-specified training/validation design with one phase 3 trial (JAVELIN Renal 101, n=603) and two phase 2 validation cohorts (NIVOREN n=278, SURF n=170), using the Contal–O'Quigley method to derive the 180 ng/mL cut-off and locking it for validation; multivariable Cox adjusting for IMDC and time-dependent AUC with linearity checks via restricted cubic splines strengthen rigor. However, no a priori power calculation is reported, dichotomization at the 25th percentile loses information, and the statistical approach throughout the microbiome analyses explicitly reports unadjusted P values with the authors acknowledging that 'none of the associations presented adjusted P values with Benjamini–Hochberg correction lower than 0.2.' Figure 4a uses a paired t-test on skewed Luminex data where a signed-rank approach would be more defensible, and missing-data handling and reasons for sample availability varying by consent/volume are not quantified. Validation PFS was not significant in either cohort, mitigating the robustness of the prognostic claim beyond OS.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prognostic biomarker analysis of prospectively collected plasma from one phase 3 RCT (JAVELIN Renal 101) and two phase 2 cohorts with external validation — functionally an individual cohort/prognostic biomarker study, mapping to Oxford 2b. Clinical relevance is substantive: endpoints are patient-centered (OS, PFS), the biomarker is independent of IMDC after adjustment (HR 2.11 for OS in NIVOREN), and the translational path to microbiota-directed interventions is concrete, with an ongoing phase 1 trial (NCT05865730) of Oncobax AK cited. The authors appropriately temper enthusiasm — AUC improvement over IMDC is modest (0.72 vs 0.68) and avelumab/nivolumab monotherapy regimens are less relevant to current practice.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the applicable checklist for this prognostic biomarker evaluation. Patient characteristics, assay platform (Bio-Plex 200, R&D LXSAHM), cut-off derivation, Cox modeling and both univariable and adjusted estimates with 95% CIs are reported, but a REMARK-style patient flow diagram, pre-specified analysis plan registration for the biomarker substudy, explicit handling of missing samples, and model calibration are not shown. Underlying trial protocols and source data per figure are referenced; however, formal repository deposition identifiers for the metagenomic sequencing reads (e.g., SRA/ENA accessions) and analytical code are not provided in the retained text — only generic 'Source data' tags and a redacted data/code availability section remain.

novelty_literature.justification: The conceptual claim that sMAdCAM-1 reflects a microbiota-driven gut immune checkpoint relevant to immunotherapy outcomes was established by the authors' prior Science 2023 paper (ref 25, Fidelle et al.), including initial RCC, lung and urothelial data. The current study extends that work by (i) validating a locked 180 ng/mL cut-off derived in a large phase 3 RCT, (ii) demonstrating prognostic value for both TKI and ICI-based regimens in mRCC specifically, and (iii) linking longitudinal pharmacodynamics to Enterocloster dysbiosis across the ONCOBIOME meta-cohort. This is a meaningful methodological and empirical extension in a disease-specific setting rather than a first-in-class mechanistic discovery, so novelty is moderate and incremental.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured: the Introduction frames the MAdCAM-1–α4β7 axis clearly, Methods are organized by cohort, and the Discussion explicitly enumerates four limitations including generalizability, comorbidities, modest incremental AUC and dated regimen choices. Table 1 integrates all three cohorts coherently and figure captions are quantitative with per-panel Ns. Minor issues include duplicated figure caption blocks in the submitted text, some long run-on sentences in the Results, and occasional inconsistency between 'MAdCAM-1' and 'sMAdCAM-1' in correlation descriptions. Overall the abstract accurately summarizes the quantitative claims of the paper.

key_strengths: Locked 180 ng/mL cut-off derived in a phase 3 training cohort (JAVELIN Renal 101, n=603) and validated in two independent prospective cohorts (NIVOREN, SURF), totaling 1,051 patients

sMAdCAM-1 remained independently prognostic for OS after adjustment for IMDC and antibiotic use (HR 2.11, 95% CI 1.27–3.49 in NIVOREN) and improved time-dependent AUC vs IMDC alone (0.72 vs 0.68, P=0.01)
Pharmacodynamic signal differentiating ICI-containing vs TKI monotherapy therapy and persistence of low sMAdCAM-1 across cycles tied to worse PFS/OS
Mechanistic microbiome correlates with Enterocloster dominance replicated across cancer types in the ONCOBIOME meta-cohort
Candid, enumerated limitations and realistic framing of the biomarker as a tool for microbiota-targeted trials rather than a standalone assay
key_concerns: Microbiome differential-abundance analyses rely entirely on raw P values; none survive Benjamini–Hochberg at FDR<0.2, as the authors acknowledge
PFS was not validated in SURF or NIVOREN, weakening the dynamic-biomarker generalization beyond OS
Absolute incremental discrimination over IMDC is modest (ΔAUC ≈0.04) and dichotomization at the 25th percentile discards information
No power calculation, no REMARK-style flow diagram for the biomarker substudy, and limited handling of informative missingness due to sample-availability constraints
Formal repository accessions for metagenomic reads and analytical code are not evident in the retained text
Novelty is incremental to the authors' prior Fidelle et al. 2023 Science paper that first established the sMAdCAM-1/α4β7/Enterocloster framework
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, large, multi-cohort prognostic biomarker validation with credible translational implications but modest incremental novelty and discrimination. Fits comfortably in Tier 2 (JIF ~10–19) with minor revisions to address multiplicity, PFS validation discrepancies and formal data/code deposition; tier 1 is a reach given the limited ΔAUC and dependence on prior mechanistic work.
